children: shares fell 2.5% at 10.40 a.m. ET on November 16 in regular trading, the first session after a large European privacy penalty. Italy's data protection authority, the Garante, fined Meta Platforms Ireland 805 million, according to CyberInsider, after finding that Facebook's Android app accessed users' photos, videos and metadata without valid consent. Meta called the fine disproportionate and said it intends to appeal.

The order goes beyond money. The Garante found a single Android permission covered several features and that the permission notice did not disclose its use for post suggestions. Meta has 60 days to explain and justify the gallery access, must switch the feature off by default even for users who already granted access, and must report initial steps within 30 days. CyberInsider put the fine at about 0.47% of Meta's global revenue. For scale, Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26%, and guided fourth-quarter revenue to $73 billion to $76 billion.

Financially, the penalty is a rounding error; the default-off requirement is the real cost if it trims photo-based engagement and ad signals in Europe. The bigger swing factor remains spending: Meta narrowed its 2026 capex outlook to $135 billion to $145 billion. GuruFocus gives Meta a GF Score of 99/100, near-perfect across profitability, growth and balance sheet strength. Shares trade about 29% below the $886.85 GF Value, a modestly undervalued reading. Regulatory drag alone rarely closes a gap like that. The next marker is Meta's 30-day compliance report to the Garante, and whether other EU regulators follow with similar orders.

title: Meta Stocks Fall 2.5% After Italy Fines Facebook 805 Million Over Photo Access
